newsitem.title: POLAND: MANAGEMENT FIRM SUES POLISH NFI II FUND IN COURT.
newsitem.headline: MANAGEMENT FIRM SUES POLISH NFI II FUND IN COURT.

text.p: Hevelius Management, the firm which had run Poland's National Investment Fund (NFI) No. 2 until last month, has sued the fund for overdue compensation, the company said on Thursday.
Hevelius said in a statement it was demanding a fee for the last quarter of 1996.
Last month, the supervisory board of NFI No. 2, one of 15 such institutions created under Poland's mass privatisation scheme, broke the agreement with Hevelius on managing the fund.
Hevelius said the fund had no right to withdraw from the agreement, saying it had been properly running the fund.
The funds, controlling some 500 mid-size companies, have hired consortia of foreign and domestic companies to manage their firm portfolios, restructure the companies and find investors for them.
They are to be listed on the Warsaw bourse this year.
Hevelius includes NP International Holding with a 50- percent stake, Bank Gdanski, which holds a 40-percent equity, and Murray Johnstone Poland Ltd.
In November, Bank Gdanski SA said it planned to sell its stake in Hevelius, saying the move is necessary to protect its interests.
